 Saini transfers Rs 4,470 crore for welfare schemes, hikes DA by 3%
 City | Times News Network | Nov 7, 2026, 00:16 IST Haryana CM Nayab Singh Saini addresses a news conference on Friday Save Comments Share Chandigarh: Haryana chief minister Nayab Singh Saini on Friday announced a Dhanteras bonanza of Rs 4,470.77 crore, transferring funds to beneficiaries of welfare schemes and local bodies across the state. He also announced a 3% hike in dearness allowance (DA) for govt employees and dearness relief (DR) for pensioners, taking the rate from 60% to 63% with effect from July 1, 2026.
 The DA/DR revision will benefit around 2.78 lakh regular employees and 2.60 lakh pensioners, besides employees of boards, corporations and other govt organisations. It will entail an additional annual expenditure of Rs 545 crore during 2026-27.
 The biggest allocations included Rs 1,727.80 crore to urban local bodies and Rs 1,158 crore to Panchayati Raj institutions for development works. The rural grant covers 22 zila parishads, 143 panchayat samitis and 6,230 gram panchayats. With the latest release, total disbursement to municipalities during the current financial year has reached Rs 1,927.80 crore.
 Under the Deen Dayal Lado Lakshmi Yojana, the govt transferred the 13th instalment of Rs 222.52 crore to 10.59 lakh women. The cumulative disbursement under the scheme has reached Rs 2,689.15 crore. The second phase, launched on Sept 17, expanded eligibility by raising the annual family income ceiling from Rs 1 lakh to Rs 1.80 lakh.
 Another Rs 1,135.21 crore was transferred to 35.26 lakh beneficiaries under 15 social security pension schemes. The govt also released Rs 24.25 crore in LPG subsidy to 6.05 lakh women under the Har Ghar-Har Grihini Yojana.
 Additionally, Rs 202.99 crore was disbursed to 5,429 families under the Dayalu Yojana, taking cumulative assistance to Rs 3,682.83 crore for 97,655 families.

 Saini said the govt was using the Parivar Pehchan Patra database to identify eligible beneficiaries and deliver social security benefits without requiring them to apply separately.
 In another relief measure, the govt brought beekeeping under the Mukhyamantri Bagwani Bima Yojana, offering insurance cover of Rs 1,250 per bee colony and box against a premium of Rs 50, with claims of up to Rs 6.25 lakh.
